summary: No pilot or high-pressure study covers 30 wt% MEA on shifted syngas. The four natural gas studies (Isa, Tan, Halim, Salvinder) use 20 wt% or up to about 24 wt% fresh solvent with no stripper, so they give no SRD. They give no usable rich loading (Isa Table 9 does not close its mass balance) and no H2 or CH4 co-absorption data. The report's 3.46 to 4.0 GJ/t pairs two campaign minima on different bases, so carry 3.8 GJ/t, range 3.4 to 4.2 [own estimate], which is 74 MW (67 to 82 MW) at 70.4 t/h. Reboilers run at 114 to 124 C on steam near 145 C, so syngas at 120 to 130 C cannot drive them. Syngas above 135 C offers 29 MW after the LTS or 56 MW over the whole chain, and low-grade syngas suits only a stripper interheater near 102 C. MEA is defensible only as a conservative reference: IEAGHG uses aMDEA, INL uses Selexol at 0.92 GJ/t, and Tan's selection chart puts this feed in the physical solvent or hot carbonate region. The 90% is per-pass on absorber-inlet CO2, which is about 68 to 70% of syngas carbon unless tail gas is recycled. 210 MWth does not close with MEA; screening gives 219 to 235 MWth at 11.6 MWe. All 0.585 Mt/y variants stay above 0.25 Mt/y. Full evidence is in the report at report_path.

conflicts.detail: Report gives approx. 3.46 to 4.0 GJ/t from [31,32]. 3.46 is a best run at 26-28 wt% excluding heat loss. 4.0 is a minimum at 85% capture on 3.5 vol% CO2.
conflicts.resolution: Replace with 3.8, range 3.4-4.2, on a heat-loss-included reboiler basis.

conflicts.detail: Deck slide 12 notes say 11.6 MWe provides all parasitic energy. Reboiler heat of 67-82 MW appears nowhere in the 206 MWth budget.
conflicts.resolution: Add the reboiler to the energy balance and state the source of the heat.

conflicts.detail: amine_spec applies 90% to absorber feed CO2. Deck applies it to all process CO2 with 10% slip and 93.5% reduction. CH4 and CO bypass the absorber.
conflicts.resolution: Report both per-pass and plant capture. Without recycle plant capture is about 68-70%.

conflicts.detail: Proposal recycles tail gas. 31 Oct report puts it outside the boundary. 5.7 MWe purge recovery, which enables INL Case 6 recycle, is removed from the load.
conflicts.resolution: Choose one: keep recycle and 17.3 MWe, or exclude it and show lower plant capture.

conflicts.detail: amine_spec uses 1,777 kmol/h, which equals INL total plant CO2 of 2,069 ton/d, plus 395 CH4 and 197 CO. Carbon totals 2,369 kmol/h, 133% of INL. Case 6 absorber CO2 at 99% is about 1,672 kmol/h [calc].
conflicts.resolution: Rebuild feed from INL streams; Case 5 gives 1,706 kmol/h CO2 [calc].

conflicts.detail: amine_spec uses 21 bar, 35 C, 18 mol% from Chen and Ahn, with pCO2 3.78 bar. INL Case 5 flowsheet gives 26.8 bar, 40 C, 17.7 mol% and pCO2 4.74 bar.
conflicts.resolution: Use INL conditions for consistency with the 130 MMSCFD basis.

conflicts.detail: v1.7: 210 MWth, 25.1 MWth, 47%, 11.8 MWe. Deck: 206 MWth, 11.6 MWe. 31 Oct: 230 MWth, 220.4 MWth, 17.3 MWe, 39.7%. None includes the reboiler.
conflicts.resolution: Re-size with regeneration heat. Screening gives 219-249 MWth.

conflicts.detail: Slide says 206 MWth of helium heat at 900 C. Only 176.8 MWth reaches the reformer at 900 C.
conflicts.resolution: Reword; the remainder is the screening allocation for power.

conflicts.detail: Vinjarapu 2025 abstract gives 2.71 at about 83%, Table 4 gives 80%, conclusion gives 2.73. Total heat including interheater is 3.77 GJ/t [calc].
conflicts.resolution: Do not quote 2.25-2.71 as heat savings. Use only as a duty shift to lower grade heat.

conflicts.detail: Table 9 gives 0.056-0.196. Table 3 flows with Fig 10 removal imply 0.31-0.32 [calc]. Text and table also swap the alpha labels.
conflicts.resolution: Do not use as rich loading data. Use removal only.

conflicts.detail: Salvinder Table 1 mol basis vs 20 wt% text; Halim text mol/m2 vs figure mol/m3; IEAGHG stream 13 prints CH4 in the oxygen row; Isa Eqs 16, 25, 28 differ from Khan.
conflicts.resolution: Use Halim figures, read stream 13 as CH4 (balance confirms 201 kmol/h), and use Khan's equation forms.

conflicts.detail: Table 5-3 value 263.3 is steam in 1000 lb/h, which looks like duty. E-104 lists 242 MMBtu/h.
conflicts.resolution: Use 242 MMBtu/h, giving 3.64 GJ/t [calc]. The two values agree through an implied 919 Btu/lb.

decisions.question: Which solvent does the report carry as its base case?
decisions.why: Selexol at 0.92 GJ/t or aMDEA near 3.0 against MEA at 3.4-4.2 shifts low-grade heat by 47-63 MW and therefore reactor size.
decisions.default: Keep 30 wt% MEA as a stated conservative reference, and add one sensitivity each for Selexol and aMDEA.
options: Keep MEA with disclosure and sensitivities

decisions.question: Which SRD does the model carry?
decisions.why: It sets reboiler duty from 67 to 82 MW and drives heat, cost and reactor sizing.

decisions.question: Is PSA tail gas recycled to the reformer?
decisions.why: It decides whether 90% per pass is about 93% or about 68-70% of plant carbon, and whether 5.7 MWe is in the load.
decisions.default: Recycle as in INL Case 6, restore 17.3 MWe, and state per-pass and plant capture together.
options: Keep tail gas outside boundary and report 68-70% with 0.49-0.50 Mt/y

decisions.question: Where does regeneration heat come from, and at what reactor size?
decisions.why: 210 MWth has 4 MWth margin against a 23-39 MW net gap. This changes reactor scale and cost.
decisions.default: Use about 230 MWth at 11.6 MWe or about 245 MWth at 17.3 MWe, with extraction steam and INL export steam diverted, labelled as screening.
options: Keep 210 MWth and buy heat elsewhere

decisions.question: What absorber feed basis is used?
decisions.why: Current spec overstates carbon by 33% and uses 21 bar rather than INL 26.8 bar, which changes solvent rate, loads and capture accounting.
decisions.default: Rebuild from INL Case 5 streams (26.8 bar, 40 C, 17.7 mol% dry, about 1,706 kmol/h CO2), scaled to Case 6 totals.
options: Keep Chen and Ahn composition with corrected carbon balance

decisions.question: What stripper pressure is used?
decisions.why: About 1.5 bar gives about 114 C against about 122 C at 2 bar, which opens lower-grade heat but increases compression power.
decisions.default: Keep 1.9 to 2.0 bar and run 1.5 bar as a sensitivity.

gaps: No pilot of 30 wt% MEA on shifted syngas or on any H2-rich gas exists in the folder.
No stripper data exist for solvent loaded at high pressure, so SRD on syngas is an extrapolation.
H2, CH4 and CO co-absorption in MEA are not measured in any local source; values are not verified.
No 30 wt% VLE near 4.7 bar at 40-80 C locally: Aronu stops near 12-14 kPa at or below 60 C, and Wong covers 30-50 C on pure CO2.
TEV-961 Appendix A in the local PDF ends at A-59 in Case 5, and electronic Appendix G is absent, so Case 5 stands in for Case 6.
INL Selexol is a separation block with literature utilities, so 0.92 GJ/t is not a rigorous column result.
IEAGHG gives no reboiler duty; aMDEA 3.0 and split-flow MEA 2.67 GJ/t are my estimates using steam enthalpies not verified from the report.
Morgan Part 1 is not in the folder, so MellapakPlus correlation forms are missing, and Billet-Schultes CL and CG constants for project packings are not available.
Effect on reformer yield of about 184 kmol/h recycled CO2 at 90% per pass is not quantified in any local source.
MEA degradation and corrosion on oxygen-free syngas with CO present are not verified; Kwak's 79.11 mpy at the stripper bottom is the only local corrosion figure.
Sources cited in amine_spec (Chen and Ahn, Guo, Abu-Zahra, De Castro) and Sheng 2023 were not read or verified in this review.
Column hydraulics at L/G 12-15 kg/kg on 27 bar syngas are not covered by any local experiment; 4-6.5 m diameter is a screening value.
